title: What is CBERS?
hook: Brazil and China teamed up so they wouldn’t depend on other countries’ satellite images.
summary: CBERS is a Brazil–China Earth-observation satellite programme agreed in 1988; its first satellite went up in 1999.

cardBlocks.text: Without their own satellites, developing countries depended on images taken by other nations’ equipment. To change that, Brazil and China signed an agreement on 6 July 1988 between INPE, Brazil’s space research institute, and the China Academy of Space Technology (CAST) to build two remote-sensing satellites. That was the start of CBERS, the China–Brazil Earth Resources Satellite programme.

The first, CBERS-1, was launched in the early hours of 14 October 1999 on a Chinese Long March 4B rocket from the Taiyuan launch centre in China. The programme carried on: in 2002, a new agreement covered CBERS-3 and 4, with costs split half and half between the two countries.
CBERS grew out of a 1988 Brazil–China agreement; the programme’s first satellite went up in 1999.

deepDiveBlocks.text: As well as cameras, the first satellites carried a relay for Brazil’s environmental data collection system.
In 2004, the two countries also decided to build CBERS-2B, launched in 2007, which worked until early 2010. Today, cameras on CBERS-04 and CBERS-04A help produce INPE’s daily deforestation alerts.
